newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Svyazinvest stake seen broken up - reports.
newsitem.headline: Russia Svyazinvest stake seen broken up - reports.

text.p: Russia plans to divide a 25 percent stake to be auctioned in telecoms holding company AO Svyazinvest into a number of smaller packets, local media quoted State Property Committee head Alfred Kokh as saying on Wednesday.
A Kokh aide said she could not confirm or deny the reports, since Kokh was unavailable, and a spokesman for the Russian Privatisation Centre declined to comment on the remarks.

But she said a meeting to decide final terms for the auction of Svyazinvest, which has stakes in Russia's regional carriers, would be held Wednesday evening or immediately after the long holiday weekend which begins on Thursday.

Media reports were unclear whether Kokh meant the stake would be divided by quantity into smaller lots of Svyazinvest shares or whether the nature of the offering would be changed by assigning lots to stakes in specific regional carriers.
Interfax news agency quoted him as saying Russia would look for portfolio investors instead of a strategic investor, which has been the government's policy so far.

It reported him saying the auction, which is expected this year, would be similar to a special currency auction, in which lots were divided among bidders according to bid size and would raise 3-4 trillion roubles ($550-700 million) for the state.
Kokh said last week that major changes in comparison with last year's deal would be made.
Last year Italy's Stet SpA won a tender for the 25 percent stake, but the deal fell through before completion.
